results.name: Female Head from a Sarcophagus Lid
results.description:
Female Head from a Sarcophagus Lid, Found at Sidon in Lebanon. c. 450 BC. Marble from Paros. Nye Carlsberg Glyptotek (Denmark, Copenhagen). Made with Memento Beta.

The anthropoid sarcophagus originated in Egypt, but was used in Phoenicia (Lebanon) in the 5th century BC. This one has the
Egyptian false beard, but the snail curls and the thick eye lids are Greek elements. 

PS: This is the original 3D scan I have used to do the "voxel_kind_of_minecraft" model from the previous post.

results.name: Roman Well-head
results.description:
Pentelic marble well-head (puteal) decorated with four scenes of erotic pursuit: Hercules in female dress seizing Omphale, flanked on the left by a vase and on the right by a flying Cupid holding a sceptre; a female figure struggling with a male, thought to resemble Hercules; a female figure seized by a young satyr carrying a wineskin...
COL: [GAA8749](https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/G_1805-0703-227)

Diameter: 84 cm Height: 81.9cm

144 photographs, Nikon D5100, Agisoft Pro, 10 minute scan 2/5/17 by Daniel Pett. False bottom added to model in Blender.

results.name: Ranitomeya imitator (Female)
results.description:
3D scan of a female poison dart frog (*Ranitomeya imitator*) model made of sculpting clay by Iris Rubin from the Zoological Preparation unit of the NHMW. If you decide to paint your own frog digitally or after 3D printing we would love to see it!

Find out more about the NHMW [here](https://www.nhm.at/en).

results.name: Limestone Female double-faced head
results.description:
Four of these heads were discovered in 1968 built into a Hellenistic drain. They all have mortise holes top and bottom, and seem to have served as impressive ornaments in some important structure, perhaps as column capitals or more likely window balusters. Some of the ivory inlay in the eyes still remains. The three holes on the collar were probably originally intended for inlaid garment decoration or necklace, possibly in ivory.

Found in Amman Citadel.

Iron Age II, 7th century BC

**Inventory Number:** J.11688

This project was a collaboration between the [PDTRA](https://pdtra.gov.jo/Default/En), [DoA](https://doa.gov.jo/homeen.aspx), [GDH](https://globaldigitalheritage.org), and[ ACOR](https://acorjordan.org). Scanned by GDH in November 2024 using [Artec Leo](https://www.artec3d.com) scanner. The data was processed using Artec Studio 18, [Meshlab]( https://www.meshlab.net) and [Blender]( https://www.blender.org).

results.name: Head of Dystacta alticeps (Bush Tiger Mantid)
results.description:
Head of female *Dystacta alticeps* (Mantodea: Chroicopteridae)

Imaged with [scAnt](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4694713/), controlled by a Raspberry Pi and modified to house a RPi HQ cam with a Nikon EL-Nikkor 50mm 1:2.8 lens, mounted in reverse on a [Nikon RPi HQ cam adapter](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:4364692).

10,206 single photos. Focus-stacked to 126 images with [Zerene Stacker](https://www.zerenesystems.com/) (PMax). Brightness and contrast adjusted in [Fiji](https://imagej.net/software/fiji/). Reconstructed in [Meshroom](https://alicevision.org/#meshroom) with standard Meshroom settings except FeatureExtraction: Describer Types = 'sift' + 'akaze', and Texturing: Texture Downscale = '1'. Decimated to 30% of original triangles and smoothed (20 iter., factor 0.15) in [Blender](https://www.blender.org/).

Original colours were lost due to alcohol storage of the specimen.

Bush Tiger Mantid

\# PR_0320; ERC_3409

results.name: Caryatid - Ancient Greece Collection
results.description:
One caryatid from the temple of Athena on the Acropolis in Athens. This is a replica, original ones being exposed in museums in Greece but also one in the British Museum.

Limited scan. Because of the difficult environment, I was forced to take pictures from very far with almost no sight of the back. I partly reconstructed missing parts in this area and textured too. I also did some manual delighting in blender to suppress hard shadows caused by morning sunlight.


**A caryatid is a sculpted female figure serving as an architectural support taking the place of a column or a pillar supporting an entablature on her head. The Greek term karyatides literally means "maidens of Karyai", an ancient town on the Peloponnese.
[wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caryatid)**
